events.l: Nitehawk: Tally Brown, New York — Recent Restorations
events.desc: 2K restoration by the Deutsche Kinemathek “The bewigged Miss Brown, with false eyelashes capable of sending her short, round body aloft, is the most memorable raconteur and cabaret artist you’ll hear all year.” – Melissa Anderson, The Village Voice Both a loving portrait of a larger-than-life personality and a vivid record of New York’s 1970s downtown demimonde, this captivating documentary follows Tally Brown—cabaret chanteuse, underground film star, and a staple of Andy Warhol’s Factory—as she takes filmmaker Rosa von Praunheim on a tour through the grit and glamour of the city that made her. Capturing Brown’s mesmerizing performances (including her breathtaking bilingual cover of David Bowie’s “Heroes”) as well as her social world among fellow queer cult icons like Holly Woodlawn, Divine, and Taylor Mead, Tally Brown, New York is an essential snapshot of a scene that has passed into legend. (Directed by Rosa von Praunheim, 1979, 101 min., DCP, Rated NR.) Film series: Recent Restorations / Representation. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Join a member of the Brooklyn Bird Club to learn birding basics and search for the dozens of species found in the park across all seasons. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. What to Bring: Binoculars if you have them, comfortable walking shoes, water, and weather-appropriate clothing. A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Please Note : Pets are not permitted on this outing. Depending on attendance, participants may be divided into smaller groups. Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

Starring: Faye Dunaway, Peter Finch, William Holden, Robert Duvall, Beatrice Straight, Wesley Addy, Ned Beatty I’m mad as hell and I’m not going to take this anymore! Fired after twenty-five years as an anchorman on UBS, Howard Beale proclaims on his last broadcast that he was going to commit suicide and, although he doesn’t, his on-air rant of self destruction becomes an unexpected ratings sensation. Fueled by the ambitious programming executive Diana Christensen, the focus of the network takes on a new trashy but lucrative turn that is to the disappointment of the news division president Max Schumacher (Beale’s longtime friend and Christensen’s occasional lover). Forty years after release, Sidney Lumet’s satirical film about the exploitative nature of trash news television is more relevant than ever. (Directed by Sidney Lumet, 1976, 121 min., DCP, Rated R.) Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

Nitehawk: Millennium Actress — Anime After Dark
events.desc: Starring: Miyoko Shôji, Shôzô Îzuka, Mami Koyama Experience the gorgeous new restoration of what many believe to be Satoshi Kon’s ( Perfect Blue, Paprika, Tokyo Godfathers ) greatest work, Millennium Actress . When the legendary Ginei Studios shuts down, filmmaker Genya Tachibana and his assistant are tasked with interviewing its reclusive star, Chiyoko Fujiwara, who had retired from the spotlight 30 years prior. As she recounts her career, Genya and his crew are literally pulled into her memories where they witness her chance encounter with a mysterious man on the run from the police. Despite never knowing his name or his face, Chiyoko relentlessly pursues that man in a seamless blend of reality and memory that only Satoshi Kon could deliver. Boasting countless awards, including the Grand Prize in the Japan Agency of Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival, which it shared with Hayao Miyazaki’s Spirited Away , Millennium Actress is a must-see for anime fans of all ages. (Directed by Satoshi Kon, 2001, 87 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Anime After Dark / The Anniversary Party. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.l: Nitehawk: Once Upon a Time in Harlem — Adventures in Black Cinema
events.desc: A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance. For four hours, this extraordinary group – many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years – reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape. Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance. William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive. (Directed by David Greaves, 2026, 100 min., DCP, Rated PG 13.) Film series: Adventures in Black Cinema / ICYMI. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.l: Nitehawk: Shouting at the Screen — One Nite Only
events.desc: Hosted by Wyatt Cenac and Donwill, with a special guest Preceded by DJ set by Donwill in Trees Lounge The end of an era is upon us. After 15 years of shouting, we have finally lost our voices. So let’s gather one last time to watch a bit of Blaxploitation and point out some of its most utterly ridiculous tropes. It’s been an absolute joy to share these films with you and reframe that boom mic dangling from the corner of the frame, terrible fight scene or overdramatic death within the context of what it actually is: art. Our only hope is that after this event series you are a little kinder to the people at theaters who talk back at films because it just might be one of us jonesin’ for a fix. After tonight may all of your films be shout-less! (85 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: One Nite Only. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.l: Birds of a Feather, Count Together! A Family Winter Bird Count
events.desc: Who’s hiding among the bare branches? Who’s splashing in the icy waters? And whose calls can you hear on a chilly winter day? Bundle up and join Prospect Park Alliance for a fun, free birdwatching adventure as we discover the colorful and surprising world of Prospect Park’s winter birds! Inspired by the National Audubon Society’s annual Christmas Bird Count, we’re inviting families to become bird detectives, explore the park, and help count our feathered friends. Since 1900, this beloved tradition has brought people together to observe birds and contribute to research that helps protect them. Every bird counts! RSVP Search for woodpeckers, cardinals, chickadees, ducks, and other birds that spend the winter in Prospect Park. Learn to recognize them by their colors, calls, and behaviors, discover how they find food and shelter during the colder months, and see how many you can spot! Winter Bird Discovery Stations, 12 to 3 pm : Get hands-on with the wonderful world of winter birds! Discover what different birds eat, play bird identification games, and uncover the surprising ways birds stay warm during Brooklyn’s coldest months. Bird Detectives, 12 to 4 pm : Become a bird detective and explore Prospect Park at your own pace! Pick up a bird detective activity sheet and set off with your family to look for birds, listen for their calls, and discover clues about where they find food, shelter, and places to rest. How many birds can you spot? Winter Bird Count Walks, 1 pm and 3 pm : Bundle up and join Alliance Naturalists for a guided birdwatching adventure through Prospect Park! Search for winter birds, learn to recognize them, and help count the birds we spot along the way. Binoculars will be available to borrow. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No birdwatching experience or special equipment is needed. Just bring your curiosity and dress warmly for outdoor activities!

Join the Urban Park Rangers for a guided hike focused on beginner wildlife tracking and species identification. Discover how to spot and interpret the subtle clues animals leave behind — from tracks and trails to feeding signs and habitat patterns. Learn which curious creatures call Prospect Park home and how to read the landscape to find them. The walk departs from outside the Boathouse promptly at 1 pm. Learn more from the event organizer.

Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

events.l: Martin Luther King Jr. Day School Holiday in Prospect Park
events.desc: Join Prospect Park Alliance at the Prospect Park Audubon Center, LeFrak Center at Lakeside and the Tennis Center for the Martin Luther King Jr. Day School Holiday in Prospect Park! Nature Exploration, 12–4 PM Prospect Park Audubon Center, Free: prospectpark.org/audubon Make the most of winter break with a wild adventure in Prospect Park! Who’s hiding beneath the leaves? Which animals are still active in the cold? And how do plants and wildlife survive the winter? Join Prospect Park Alliance for free, family-friendly nature activities and discover a whole new side of Brooklyn’s backyard! All ages and experience levels are welcome. Dress warmly and bring your curiosity! Nature Around Us, 12–3 pm : Winter is full of surprises! Explore hands-on discovery stations, play nature games, and uncover the secrets of plants and animals during the coldest months. Investigate animal tracks, discover where wildlife finds food and shelter, and learn how trees and other plants prepare for spring. Nature Detectives, 2–3 pm : Put your detective skills to the test! Join Alliance Naturalists to investigate the animals in our collection and look for signs of wildlife outdoors. Observe how animals move and behave, discover clues about their habitats, and see what you can uncover about the creatures that share our park. Family Nature Walk, 3–4 pm : Bundle up and head outdoors with Alliance Naturalists for a winter adventure! Explore Prospect Park’s trails, search for birds and other wildlife, and discover the surprising signs of life all around us. Every season brings something new to explore! This program departs from the Boathouse promptly at 3 pm. Martin Luther King Jr. Day Holiday Tennis Program , 1–4 PM Prospect Park Tennis Center, Registration Required, $85: prospectpark.org/tennis Geared for both adults and youth, this popular Prospect Park Tennis Center clinic features a fast-paced station drill that focuses on specific skills, including serve & volley, ground strokes, approach shots and offense/defense strategies. Registration information coming soon. New to Prospect Park Tennis Center? Create a profile now . Holiday Pricing at LeFrak Center at Lakeside Skating LeFrak Center at Lakeside, Prices vary: lakeside.prospectpark.org Public sessions are open to skaters of all ages. Come with your friends, family or just enjoy the session on your own, and circle the ice while listening to the latest pop tunes. It’s a great time for skaters of all ages and experience. Enjoy special holiday pricing on January 18 for Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

events.l: Birds, Binoculars & Brooklyn! The Great Backyard Bird Count at Prospect Park
events.desc: Calling all curious kids, bird lovers, and backyard explorers! Did you know that Prospect Park is home to an incredible variety of birds, even in the middle of winter? Join Prospect Park Alliance at the Boathouse for a fun-filled celebration of our feathered Brooklyn neighbors as we participate in the Great Backyard Bird Count, an annual worldwide community science event. Families are invited to become bird detectives, try out binoculars, explore bird habitats, listen for bird calls, and discover what makes each bird unique. Help us count the birds of Prospect Park and contribute to a global effort to better understand and protect bird populations. Drop-in Activities, 1–4 pm: Binocular Boot Camp: Learn how to use binoculars through playful observation challenges before heading outside to spot birds around the Boathouse. Brooklyn Bird Bingo: Pick up a bird bingo card and search for some of Prospect Park’s winter residents, from cardinals and blue jays to ducks and woodpeckers. Beaks, Feet & Feathers: Why do ducks have webbed feet? How does a woodpecker find its food? Explore the fascinating adaptations that help birds survive through hands-on games and activities. Build a Bird-Friendly Brooklyn: Discover what birds need to thrive and explore simple ways families can help protect them in their neighborhoods, schoolyards, balconies, and community gardens. The Great Brooklyn Bird Count Board: Throughout the event, families can add their bird sightings to a giant community tally. At the end of the day, we’ll celebrate what we discovered together and share how our observations contribute to the Great Backyard Bird Count. Bird Counts, 1 pm + 3 pm: Help us count the birds of Prospect Park! Families can join guided bird counts, record their observations, and watch our community bird tally grow throughout the day. Learn how everyday observations contribute to scientific research. This program departs from the Boathouse promptly at 1 pm and 3 pm.

Join Prospect Park Alliance for free nature activities for children and families during mid-winter school break! Discover the wonders of winter in Prospect Park through hands-on exploration, wildlife observation, and outdoor adventures. Learn how plants and animals adapt to the cold and uncover the surprising amount of life that remains active throughout the winter. Nature Around Us , 12–3 pm : Explore the wonders of winter through seasonal discovery stations, nature games, and hands-on activities. Investigate animal tracks, discover how plants and animals survive freezing temperatures, and learn where wildlife finds food and shelter during the colder months. Explore the fascinating adaptations that help Prospect Park’s wildlife thrive all winter long. Nature Detectives, 2 – 3 pm : Put your observation skills to the test! Join Alliance Naturalists to investigate the animals in our collection and search for wildlife outside the Boathouse. Look closely at animal behaviors, discover clues about how animals live, and learn to identify the signs of wildlife all around us. This program begins promptly at 2 pm. Winter Wilderness Walk, 3 – 4 pm : Bundle up and join Alliance Naturalists for a guided winter adventure along Prospect Park’s nature trails. Look for animal tracks and other signs of wildlife, discover how trees and plants survive the cold, and search for birds and other animals that remain active throughout the winter. Experience the quieter side of Prospect Park and discover that nature never really takes a winter break! This program departs from the Boathouse promptly at 3 pm.

Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Join a member of the Brooklyn Bird Club to learn birding basics and search for the dozens of species found in the park across all seasons. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. What to Bring: Binoculars if you have them, comfortable walking shoes, water, and weather-appropriate clothing. A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Please Note : Pets are not permitted on this outing. Depending on attendance, participants may be divided into smaller groups. Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

events.l: That Feeling In Your Gut: Is This the Right School? (February 2027)
events.desc: 6:30 PM to 8:30 PM. In this webinar, Sarah Birnbaum of New York Special Needs Support will be joined by attorney Greg Cangiano of Skyer Law and neuropsychologists Dr. Laura Tagliareni and Dr. David Salsberg of PALS. events.l: NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hospital Parkinson’s and Other Movement Disorders CME
events.desc: NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hospital Dr. Miran Salgado, Chief of Neurosciences and Dr. Michael Kapplitt, Neurosurgeon at Weill Cornell Medicine Parkinson’s and Other Movement Disorders CME 1st Fridays of the Month / 12pm – 1pm / Zoom Presented by: Dr. Miran Salgado and Dr. Michael Kaplitt CME program will meet on these dates: November 6, December 4, January 1, February 5, March 5, April 2, May 7, June 4 Objectives: At the completion of this activity, participants should be able to: Be able to definitively diagnose Parkinson’s, Parkinsonism, and atypical Parkinson’s DisordersKnow appropriate neurosurgical interventions that are available for treatment of movement disordersRecognize the importance of interdisciplinary team approach and how to utilize the different disciplines to maximize care and treatment for patients with Parkinson’s Disease Target Audience: Physicians in practice, Physician assistants, Physicians in training and Medical Students This activity is sponsored by the Department of Neurosciences. Please contact Rose Brown, LMSW, for Zoom information at eqa9001@nyp.org or 646-704-1792. Accreditation Statement NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital is accredited by The Medical Society of the State of New York to provide continuing medical education for physicians. New York Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital designates this live activity for a maximum of 1 AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™. Physicians should claim only the credit commensurate with the extent of their participation in the activity. Disclosure Statement The Medical Society of The State of New York relies upon planners and faculty participants in its CME activities to provide educational information that is objective and free of bias. In this spirit and in accordance with the guidelines of MSSNY and the ACCME, all speakers and planners for CME activities must disclose any relevant financial relationships with commercial interests whose products, devices or services may be discussed in the content of a CME activity, that might be perceived as a real or apparent conflict of interest. Any discussion of investigational or unlabeled uses of a product will be identified. The planners and faculty participants do not have any financial arrangements or affiliations with any ineligible companies whose products, research or services may be discussed in these materials. Funding Statement No commercial funding has been accepted for the activity.

events.l: NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hospital Parkinson’s and Other Movement Disorders CME
events.desc: NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hospital Dr. Miran Salgado, Chief of Neurosciences and Dr. Michael Kapplitt, Neurosurgeon at Weill Cornell Medicine Parkinson’s and Other Movement Disorders CME 1st Fridays of the Month / 12pm – 1pm / Zoom Presented by: Dr. Miran Salgado and Dr. Michael Kaplitt CME program will meet on these dates: November 6, December 4, January 1, February 5, March 5, April 2, May 7, June 4 Objectives: At the completion of this activity, participants should be able to: Be able to definitively diagnose Parkinson’s, Parkinsonism, and atypical Parkinson’s DisordersKnow appropriate neurosurgical interventions that are available for treatment of movement disordersRecognize the importance of interdisciplinary team approach and how to utilize the different disciplines to maximize care and treatment for patients with Parkinson’s Disease Target Audience: Physicians in practice, Physician assistants, Physicians in training and Medical Students This activity is sponsored by the Department of Neurosciences. Please contact Rose Brown, LMSW, for Zoom information at eqa9001@nyp.org or 646-704-1792. Accreditation Statement NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital is accredited by The Medical Society of the State of New York to provide continuing medical education for physicians. New York Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital designates this live activity for a maximum of 1 AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™. Physicians should claim only the credit commensurate with the extent of their participation in the activity. Disclosure Statement The Medical Society of The State of New York relies upon planners and faculty participants in its CME activities to provide educational information that is objective and free of bias. In this spirit and in accordance with the guidelines of MSSNY and the ACCME, all speakers and planners for CME activities must disclose any relevant financial relationships with commercial interests whose products, devices or services may be discussed in the content of a CME activity, that might be perceived as a real or apparent conflict of interest. Any discussion of investigational or unlabeled uses of a product will be identified. The planners and faculty participants do not have any financial arrangements or affiliations with any ineligible companies whose products, research or services may be discussed in these materials. Funding Statement No commercial funding has been accepted for the activity.

Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
